summary.headline: Bluspring Q2 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to ₹1,250 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to ₹67 crore, with margin at 5.4%, excluding Founded.
summary.overview: Ex-Founded, revenue crossed ₹1,000 crore for the first time at ₹1,250 crore (+49% YoY, +34% QoQ), supported by full-quarter STIAC consolidation and LSE SkyChef from August. Quarterly EBITDA rose 130% YoY to ₹67 crore and PAT rose 95% to ₹32 crore, with margins expanding across all three segments. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of revenue above ₹4,700 crore and EBITDA above ₹200 crore. Founded losses narrowed to ₹12 crore from ₹14 crore QoQ, with management targeting near break-even by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Smart Infra, Energy & Engineering (formerly Telecom & Industrials)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹449 crore (+189% YoY, +100% QoQ), EBITDA margin 10.9% (+266 bps YoY); 16 new contracts with ~₹641 crore annual contract value mobilised in the quarter. Management says STIAC contributes ~₹280 crore revenue and ~₹30 crore profit in the period.

segments.name: Facility & Food Services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹670 crore (+283% YoY, +136% QoQ), EBITDA margin 4.7% (+72 bps YoY). H1 EBITDA ₹52 crore (+32% YoY) despite food-input inflation. LSE SkyChef flight catering at Bangalore airport (concession to 2039) consolidated from August; contributed ~₹18 crore revenue and ~₹4-5 crore EBITDA.

segments.name: Security Services
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 3.2% (+19 bps YoY). Management is pursuing a turnaround and is reporting it separately to target market margins of 4-4.5%.

segments.name: Founded (excluded from figures)
segments.commentary: Q2 sales ₹30 crore (+62% YoY, +19% QoQ); EBITDA loss ₹12 crore. Management expects H2 burn of ₹20-23 crore (about 50% lower than H1's ₹26 crore) and break-even around Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue above ₹4,700 crore and EBITDA above ₹200 crore reiterated; management says EBITDA target looks comfortably achievable, with Q3 expected to exceed Q2 EBITDA.
Organic growth of 18-20% targeted for FY28 on the enlarged base; management aims to sustain this through FY30-FY32 with margin expansion.
Tax rate guidance of 22% for FY27 reiterated despite H1 ETR of around 18%, per management.
Working capital days expected to settle near 40 days for FY27.
Founded targeted for near break-even exit of Q4 FY27 and possible partial monetisation of the investment and recovery of loans.
capex_capacity: LSE SkyChef Bangalore airport kitchen: revenue to rise from ~₹100-110 crore towards ₹150-200 crore on higher flight volumes; annualised margin 17-18%; concession runs to 2039.
Two acquisitions in H1 (STIAC and LSE SkyChef) cost ~₹340 crore, of which ~₹300 crore funded by acquisition debt (~₹280 crore remaining on books); acquired entities brought ~₹188 crore cash balance.
Q2 D&A rose to ₹16 crore from ₹10 crore in Q1, driven by amortisation of intangibles and depreciation from the two acquisitions.
Management says no active acquisition in the pipeline; focus is on integrating the two acquired businesses.
demand_pricing: Management cites India greenfield FDI of ~US$351 bn over 2021-25 (per BCG) and power generation investment of ₹23-26 lakh crore over the next five years; metals and mining investment of ₹7.5-9 lakh crore expected.
Top 30 clients contribute 53% of revenue; industrial segment share of revenue rose to 37%; energy/industrial share is targeted to rise above 50% by year end (transcript says '1-3', likely >50%).
Workforce above 100,000, with 8,000+ added in H1 (including ~2,800 via acquisitions).
Cross-selling of STIAC power-plant O&M with facility, food and security services is the stated next growth lever; management is pursuing end-to-end contracts.
Founded: sales need to reach ~₹38-40 crore (P&L revenue ~₹30-33 crore) for break-even.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy to unlock next leg of growth on the larger base, and where acquisitions of STIAC and LSE add value.
qa_highlights.answer: Management says PAT and EPS grew 95-96% and the business has roughly doubled in profitability; growth from here is incremental. It reiterated the listing-day target of ~₹7,000 crore organisation by FY30 and said it is ahead of timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Founded: is the burn reduction on plan, and what sales are needed to break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Founded is on plan: sales reached ₹30 crore, and break-even needs ~₹30-33 crore of P&L revenue, i.e. ~₹38-40 crore of sales, targeted by Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be debt free by year end?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Net debt is ₹126 crore now; acquisition debt of ~₹150 crore is to be repaid, and average debt including working capital borrowing is expected at ₹150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any further acquisition in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No active acquisition is in the pipeline. Management is focused on integration and will look for quality assets with EBITDA-margin and ROE accretion, plus geographic diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses rose to ₹253 crore; what drives it and what is the H2 run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly STIAC subcontracting, with the rest telecom subcontracting. Management will report subcontracting as a separate line item and expects other expenses at similar levels in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: gross DSO appears around 90 days; how does it reconcile to ~38 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says net working capital days are 38 and expected at ~40 for FY27, with customer payment terms of 60-75 days; gross DSO is not the relevant metric.

qa_highlights.question: LSE SkyChef: long-term rationale, margin and exclusivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the kitchen earns 17-18% annualised margins, provides a niche entry into flight catering with a 15-year concession, and no exclusivity exists; airport tenders are competitive, with airline contracts of 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Acquisition debt (~₹280 crore on books as stated in Q&A) and rising finance costs under tighter liquidity; repayment pace to ₹150 crore by year-end.
Founded burn: H2 burn guided at ₹20-23 crore and break-even by Q4 FY27 must be delivered.
Integration load of STIAC and LSE SkyChef on management bandwidth.
Tax rate: H1 ETR around 18% vs 22% FY27 guidance; the reconciliation was not clear on the call.
Q3 EBITDA must exceed Q2 to support the >₹200 crore FY27 target.
Working capital days drift toward 40 days as large mobilisations ramp.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and the FY27 guidance, with Founded progress presented as on plan. Somewhat evasive on specific numbers, including the FY27 EBITDA beyond ₹200 crore and the acquisition pipeline.
key_quotes: Revenue for the quarter jumped 49% year on year to 1250 crores, crossing the 1000 crores mark for the first time.
we remain firmly confident of achieving our FY 27 guidance of crossing 4,700 crores in revenue, crossing EBITDA of 200 crores,
So founded is exactly going as per plan.
We are moving towards an outcome led model and with addition of STIAD and LST, Skyshifts.
